trust_decision.summary: The unauthenticated /api/video request is trusted only if the caller-supplied `url` resolves inside the configured video `folder`; the decision is made at the HTTP boundary by a new assertSafeAssetSource check called from getRequest and postRequest, never inside the asset functions that actually open the file.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the /api/video request handler, so an engineer opens getRequest/postRequest and sees `getAsset(url)` and `createAsset(url)` called on the raw query/body value, with getAssetConfigPath appending `.json` and loadAsset reading it from disk (src/assets.ts:54-56).

fix_sites.entry_point: GET /api/video — App Router `GET` export (src/request-handler.ts:7-13) and Pages Router `GET` on the default handler (src/request-handler.ts:24-34), query parameter `url`
POST /api/video — App Router `POST` export (src/request-handler.ts:16-21) and Pages Router `POST` on the default handler (src/request-handler.ts:26-30), JSON body field `url`
public API: new exported `assertSafeAssetSource(url)`, shipped through the package `./dist/*` export (package.json:42)
public API: `isRemote`, used by getAssetPath (src/assets.ts:59) and by every provider's uploadLocalFile

O3_reason_to_dismiss: getAsset/createAsset/updateAsset are library functions for trusted callers (CLI, webpack loader, provider callbacks), so containment belongs on the unauthenticated route and not in the asset API — which also lets the loader keep writing asset JSON outside `videos/`.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Remote http(s) source URLs are a supported feature: getAssetPath maps them into the folder through `remoteSourceAssetPath` and containment must short-circuit on them (the published fix had to make `isRemote` case-insensitive so `HTTPS://…` keeps working). A containment check pushed into createAsset would also break the webpack loader, which deliberately creates asset JSON next to video files imported from anywhere in the source tree, and a naive `rel.startsWith('..')` check rejects a legitimate file inside the folder named e.g. `videos/..foo.mp4`.

O6_input_shapes: bare relative path inside the folder (`videos/foo.mp4`)
nested relative path inside the folder (`videos/sub/dir/foo.mp4`)
traversal that goes through the folder and back out (`videos/../package`)
path exactly equal to the folder itself (`videos`)
http/https remote URL (containment bypassed by design)
uppercase scheme remote URL (`HTTPS://…`), handled by the isRemote flags change

O8_uncovered_routes.route: webpack/turbopack loader creates and reads the asset config for `this.resourcePath` with no folder containment — the imported source file may live anywhere in the tree
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: build-time module graph, not request input; the import path is chosen by the app author, so it is trusted
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: other subsystem in the same package (build loader vs HTTP handler), reached through createAsset in src/assets.ts

O8_uncovered_routes.route: remote URL: getAssetPath does `path.join(folder, remoteSourceAssetPath(url))` with an app-supplied mapper, and assertSafeAssetSource returns early for any http(s) URL, so a mapper that returns traversal escapes the folder
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: `remoteSourceAssetPath` is an owner-supplied config function (src/config.ts:33), so its output is trusted configuration rather than attacker input
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the check, but the trusted-value hook is declared in src/config.ts:33 and consumed in the sink path builder

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third route export (another verb, or a second path such as the configurable '/api/video-files') that calls getAsset/postRequest without the guard
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the package already ships three route entry points into the same two functions, the route path is configurable (src/config.ts:88, exercised as '/api/video-files' in tests/with-next-video.test.ts:60) and two router styles are documented, so adding one more export is a small, natural change

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an updateAsset-backed route that takes `originalFilePath` from a request or from the stored asset instead of validating it
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: every provider handler already re-enters updateAsset(asset.originalFilePath) → getAsset(filePath), so a maintainer reusing that pattern from a request reproduces the same sink one file away

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second path-key mapper (asset key / poster / subtitle path) that joins a user-derived value onto `folder` with no containment
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: createAssetKey and remoteSourceAssetPath already demonstrate the 'join a derived value onto folder' pattern, and generateAssetKey is another owner-supplied hook, so a poster or subtitle variant would be written the same way and look out of scope

O9_family: arbitrary file read via path traversal (CWE-200 information exposure, CWE-22 unprotected path resolution)

O10_build.toolchain: Node 22 + npm; tsc for type emission, esbuild for the ESM and CJS bundles (package.json:59-60), tsx + node:test for tests
O10_build.project_tests: `npm test` runs tests/**/*.test.ts under node --test via tsx (package.json:64); tests/config.test.ts covers getVideoConfig defaults and tests/video-handler.test.ts covers handler plumbing, but at the pinned commit there is no test for the request handler, asset path resolution or containment — the fix adds tests/assets.test.ts as a new file

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: add a `url.startsWith('..')` / `includes('..')` traversal regex to the two handler calls (or reject anything not already under `videos/`), which leaves getAsset/createAsset, the loader path and remote-URL mapping open and 404s legitimate absolute-inside-folder and uppercase-scheme remote sources.

out_of_scope_notes: The Pages Router route file documented at README.md:303-304 is not present in the tree; only the App Router example exists at examples/default-provider/app/api/video/route.js:1.
Provider upload code (mux/amazon-s3/cloudflare-r2/backblaze/vercel-blob) was read only to confirm it consumes `asset.originalFilePath`; no provider-specific behaviour was pursued.
